title: Related-Tweak Algebraic-Attack Bound for small-pSquare
summary: After full tweak absorption, 8 plus 4 times tau extra rounds are conjectured to stop related-tweak algebraic attacks on small-pSquare; establishing this for tau 1 or 2 remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the generalized Feistel cipher construction used for small-pSquare, related-tweak algebraic attacks are conjectured to be prevented when, after the tweak has been fully absorbed, the cipher includes $8+4\tau$ extra rounds, equivalently $2+\tau$ extra steps, for $\tau\in\{1,2\}$; the unresolved task is to establish this conjectured bound. The motivating limitation is that an attacker is considered unable to solve a system of equations in the tweaks covering more than 12 rounds, or equivalently 3 steps, after full tweak absorption. This algebraic bound is separate from the larger extra-step bounds stated for preventing related-tweak statistical attacks, namely 9 and 12 for $\tau=1$ and $\tau=2$, respectively.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of the small-pSquare generalized Feistel cipher under related tweaks.
assumptions: The tweak has been fully absorbed before the extra-round margin.
An attacker is considered unable to solve tweak-equation systems covering more than 12 rounds, equivalently 3 steps.
parameters: τ ∈ {1, 2}: indexes the two conjectured extra-round and extra-step margins
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish that 8+4τ extra rounds, equivalently 2+τ extra steps, prevent related-tweak algebraic attacks for τ∈{1,2} after full tweak absorption.

progress.summary: The paper explicitly states the sufficiency bound as a conjecture, motivated by the presumed infeasibility of solving tweak-equation systems spanning more than 12 rounds after absorption. It notes that tightness is unnecessary because related-tweak statistical attacks require larger margins.
